Lightning struck a home near the corner of Dunn Avenue and U.S. Highway 1. Extensive structural damage occurred. The cost of damage was estimated.
Several trees were blown down in Ratliff.
Numerous power lines were blown down in Springfield and Arlington.
Several trees were blown down along U.S. Highway 301 and on Swallowfork Avenue.
Quarter size hail was reported at Belfort and J. Turner Butler Blvd. Penny size hail was reported at San Jose Blvd. near Interstate 295.
Nickel size hail was reported in Callahan. The time of the event was based on radar.
A logde near downtown Georgetown reported penny size hail. The time of the event was based on radar.

Lightning caused a house fire on Birds Nest Lane on the west side of Jacksonville. Firefighters had the fire under control in 20 minutes. The time of the event was based on radar. The cost of damage was estimated.

Lightning caused a house fire on Ripple Rush Drive North. A 6 foot by 3 foot hole was created in the roof. Firefighters had the fire under control within 20 minutes. The time of the event was based on radar and the cost of damage was estimated.

A waterspout over the northern St. Johns River moved onshore as a tornado in the Riverside area of Jacksonville near Stockton Street and Post Street. Several trees were blown down and two trees fell on vehicles. Minor property damage occurred.
Winds were estimated between 50 and 60 mph at a sports shop in Hastings.
Numerous power lines were blown down in Broxton and a tree was blown down on a vehicle.
Trees were blown down near Blythe Island.
Numerous trees were blown down over St. Simons Island.
Trees were blown down near Dover Bluff.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were estimated.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down near Kingsland.
Trees were blown down along Wildcat Drive near the high school in Kingsland. The time of the event was based on radar.
Numerous power lines were blown down across eastern Charlton county.

events.cz_name: FERNANDINA BEACH TO ST AUGUSTINE FL 20 TO 60NM

events.event_narrative: A spotter reported penny size hail along A1A as he was driving into Amelia Island.

Heavy rainfall began in Flagler County on Sunday, May 17th associated with a cold frontal passage with between one and three inches of rain falling by Monday morning.  The rainfall increased on Monday with four and a half inches having fallen by 3 p.m. EDT/2 p.m. EST. Due to moist antecedent ground conditions flooding began quickly with County Road 35 west of Bunnell washed out near State Road 100. By Tuesday morning, the 19th, up to eleven and a half inches of rain had fallen with continuing flooding problems continuing. Heavy rainfall continued on Wednesday with up to 24 inches of rain having fallen since Sunday at the Fair Grounds. The rain finally began to slowly taper off on the 21st and 22nd; however, by the end of the event up to 28 inches of rainfall was reported by the school staff in downtown Bunnell (the County Seat). Extensive flooding was reported to multiple roads in Daytona North with over three feet of water on some. Several residents had to be rescued from flooded homes in that area. Significant roads that were reported as having been flooded and closed are County Road 75, County Road 65, Forest Park  Rd, Tangerine Rd,  County Road 15,  and Water Oak Road. In western Flagler County including Deanville, Andulusia, Cody���s Corner ���massive flooding��� of agricultural property was reported with many fields resembling lakes. Many side roads were reported as being underwater including Otis Stone Hunter Road, Hardgrove Grade (west of the Florida East Coast railroad tracks).
A large oak tree fell on a gas line of a residential structure due to heavy rain and saturated ground conditions.
A Cooperative Observer reported three inches of rain in a twenty four hour period.
A Cooperative Observer reported 3.69 inches of rain in a twenty four hour period ending at 6:00 a.m. EDT or 5:00 a.m. EST.
The general public reported a funnel cloud which dissipated before reaching the ground.
A Sheriff���s Deputy reported a funnel cloud over western Putnam County.
A section of King Street between Ponce De Leon Blvd. and Riberia Road was closed due to flooding as a result of heavy rainfall and an above normal high tide.
A Cooperative Observer measured 5.51 inches of rain during the 24 hour period from May 19th through May 20th at 5:00 a.m. EST or 6:00 a.m. EDT.

Flooding was been reported in homes on the Westside of Jacksonville on 105th Street. 2 inches of standing water was reported in some homes near the Ramona Road Flea Market. Later that afternoon McCoys Creek flooded with McCoys Creek Road and portions of Kings Street shut down. Also several homes in the 9000 block of Hecksher Drive were flooded during the evening.

Several streets near downtown wee closed due to flooding. Major areas closed were the 800 to 900 block of Market Street, the 800 to 900 block of Hubbard Street and the 000 to 100 block of Orange Street. Also portions of Lem Turner Road were closed due to flooding.

A local surf shop reporting eight foot breakers at 6:00 a.m. EST and Park rangers reported moderate beach erosion at Talbot Island State Park during the morning. Some boards were removed by wave action from the Jacksonville Beach Pier; however, these boards were designed to break off in high surf to avoid damage to the pier structure.  High surf of five to seven feet for the near shore breakers and seven to ten feet for the offshore breakers  was reported by and National Weather Service employee during the afternoon.  A strong long shore current of approximately three to four knots was also reported.
Significant beach erosion was reported at Fort Clinch. There was barely space for a vehicle on a normally wide beach. Breakers of six to seven feet were estimated at that time.
High surf was reported by the public with wave action completely covering the beach and washing up into the dune line. No beach was visible at the time of the report.
Minor beach erosion with breakers of six feet were reported during the morning.
The Jacksonville Beach Pier wind gage measured a 54 mph winds gust while a National Weather Service employee was on the pier. Some minor damage to the pier bait house.
Lightning struck the construction crane on the Flagler Beach Pier. Four workers received a slight electric jolt.
Spotters across the county reported high daily rainfall amounts. A spotter in South Central Palm Coast measured 5.00 inches of rainfall and another in West Central Palm Coast measured 3.30 inches.
Power lines were blown down west of Hortense along Highway 32.
Power lines were blown down near Hoboken.
Metal construction signs were blown down along the Interstate 95 construction zone. One sign struck a semi-truck tractor trailer and significantly damaged the windshield.
Power lines were blown down along Carswell Avenue.

events.cz_name: FERNANDINA BEACH TO ST AUGUSTINE FL 20 TO 60NM

events.event_narrative: Nickel to quarter size hail was reported by a retired NWS employee.
A motel in downtown Ocala reported dime to penny size hail. The time of the event was based on radar.
Power lines were blown down along Kinlaw Road.
Trees were blown down along Linda Street.
Trees were blown down and blocked a road near Interstate 95. The time of the event was based on radar.
Power lines were blown down along William Burgess Road.
Wind gusts were estimated to be 55 to 60 mph in west Palm Coast.
Power lines were blown down near the Daytona North subdivision.
Pea to penny size hail was reported with gusty winds.
Pea to nickel size hail fell along Monument Road.
Nickel size hail covered the ground at Atlantic Boulevard and University Boulevard.
Two houses on the 5000 block of Hecksher Drive sustained damage from fallen trees due to thunderstorm wind gusts. One house had severe damage to its backside from thunderstorm wind gusts.
A home on Russell Drive was struck by lightning with minimal damage reported. Cost of damage was estimated.
A house on Buffalo Bill Drive was struck by lightning with minimal damage reported. The cost of damage was estimated.
A funnel cloud was spotted about a half mile offshore about a half mile south of Fourth Street.

A REACT HAM operator estimated three inches of rainfall in 30 minutes. West central Palm Street flooded. The Flagler County Sheriffs office reported one foot of water on Belle Terrie Parkway in central Palm Coast. About 1.75 inches of rainfall was measured from a Grand Haven CERT member in Eastern Palm Coast within 45 minutes. About 2.8 inches of rainfall fell in 45 minutes.
Three inch branches were breaking off of trees.
Reports were received from 890 Florida Power and Light customers without power in Grand Haven due to downed power lines from thunderstorm winds.
Palm Coast CERT members estimated wind gusts to 60 mph in West-Central Palm Coast.
Lightning struck homes in Palm Coast and Flagler Beach. Brush fires were also reported. The cost of damage was estimated.
A funnel cloud was sighted and persisted for about 1 minute.
A funnel cloud was reported by an off-duty NWS employee.
An off duty NWS employee reported that there was street flooding at South Beach Parkway and 16th Avenue. Doppler radar estimated that there was about 2 inches of storm total rainfall in the area.
The ASOS at the Gainesville Regional Airport measured a wind gust to 61 mph.
A spotter measured 2.65 inches of rainfall in 1 hour and 45 minutes near Town Center Blvd. and U.S. Highway 17.

Lightning struck a cabinet store named Henry's Cabinets in St. Marys. Numerous explosions occurred due to lacquer's and other chemicals exploding inside the shop. All persons evacuated safely with no injuries.  The shop was destroyed. The cost of damage was estimated.
Penny size hail was reported along Harry Driggers Blvd.
Numerous trees were blown down across the area.
Law enforcement reported trees were blown down.
A spotter reported strong winds and trees blown down.
Trees were blown down near Brunswick.
Numerous trees were blown down across the eastern portions of Glynn County.
Powerlines were blown down in the St. Marys area.
Horseshoe Farms reported dime to penny size hail with estimated wind gusts to 50 mph.
The EOC measured 0.87 inches of rainfall in thirty minutes.

events.cz_name: ST AUGUSTINE TO FLAGLER BEACH FL OUT 20NM
events.event_narrative: The St. Augustine C-man station measured a thunderstorm wind gust to 48 mph.

Heavy Rainfall over a two week period, but more significantly extremely heavy rainfall over a 36 hour period pushed Forks Creek into flood. Tree debris left over from clear cutting of local tree farms was damming against the bridge and the Ware County Public Works Department had to use two cranes to move the debris from the upstream side of the Forks Road Bridge to the downstream side to prevent  potential damage to the bridge.

The Satilla River entered flood on April 1st 2009 due to heavy rainfall over the preceding two weeks, but more specifically extreme rainfall over the prior 35 hours. Several small communities with mobile homes were flooded with an unknown damage amount.  The river crested in Waycross on April 5th approximately 15:30 EST with crest of 22.4 feet, flood stage being 16 feet.

Heavy rainfall caused street flooding in downtown Bunnell along the east side of State Road 100 between Pine Street and Peach Street. The water was 6 inches deep along portions of Highway 1 and State Road 100, as well as along some side streets.
Daily rainfall amounts across southern, central and eastern Flagler county ranged generally from 1 to 4 inches. Four inches was measured in downtown Bunnell and at the county fairgrounds.

Flooding occurred along Riverside Avenue near St. Vincent's Hospital toward Interstate 95. The water was 8 inches deep in some areas. A forecaster a NAS Jacksonville measured 1.81 inches of rainfall in 20 minutes.  From 3:55 pm local time to 4:58 pm local time, NAS Jacksonville measured a total of 3.19 inches.

Spotters reported significant flooding mainly off of Blanding Blvd. from Orange Park toward Middleburg. Culverts were overflowed on streets with overflow water moving very quickly. Significant soil erosion occurred along Johns Avenue, and a fence was washed down. Water also flooded a car along Johns Avenue. Old Jennings Road was flooded from Blanding Blvd (State Road 21) to Brannon Field Road, and along portions of Buggy Whip Trail. Tynes Road was also flooded. A spotter measured 5.74 inches of rainfall in two hours near Arora and Blanding Blvd. Doppler radar storm total amounts indicated about 4 to 5 inches over the area.

Various portions of Palm Coast had significant rainfall amounts. A spotter about 3 miles north of Palm Coast measured 5 inches of rainfall between 2 pm and 5 pm, and this spotter had a 2 day rainfall of 8 inches. The emergency management office measured 5.05 inches of rainfall between 2 pm and 4:52 pm. Street flooding was reported on Belle Terre Parkway, Palm Coast Parkway and Laramie Lane. Water was 6 inches deep in many areas along these roads.
Lightning struck a 12 year old male near the Flagler Beach Pier. He was struck unconcious and partially paralyzed. He was air-lifted to a trama center.
Lightning struck and charred a fence.  The cost of damage was estimated and the timing of the event based on radar.
A spotter reported golfball size hail in Dixie Union.
An employee at a gas station near Highways 21 and 26 in downtown Melrose estimated wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph. Power outages were also reported in the area. The time of the event was based on radar.
A tree was blown down across Highway 129 near Interstate 75. The time of the event was based on radar.
A tree was blown down across 74th Terrace on the north side of Live Oak. The time of the event was based on radar.
A tree was blown down across Country Road 108.
Dispatch reported power lines blown down near the Intersection of Washington Avenue and Elm Street. Time of based on radar imagery.
A spotter reported two trees and a lot of debris blown down near the intersection of County Road 208 and State Road 13A in Bakersville. The time was based on radar.
Eight to nine foot breakers were observed at Flagler Beach. The Flalger Beach pier was closed at 11 am. At that time, 5 to 7 foot breakers were occurring inside the sandbar.
Breakers of 4 to 6 feet were reported outside the sandbar with 3 to 5 foot breakers inside.
Breakers of 6 to 8 feet were reported inside the sandbar with 3 to 5 feet inside near Vilano Beach.
A spotter reported a tree and debris blown down about 2 miles north of the intersection of County Road 305 and State Road 13A near Elkton. The time of the event was based on radar.
The public reported a funnel cloud that lifted back into the cloud base.
A post office carrier reported trees blown down near Gilchrist Park. The time of the event was based on radar.
A tree limb was blown down on Crescent Street. The time of the event was based on radar.
Lifeguards reported breaker heights of at least 6 feet at Hanna Park.
Lifeguards reported breaker heights of 6-7 feet at Flagler Beach.

Glynn County, Georgia Emergency Management reported that Chapel Crossing Road had to be closed during the afternoon of the 1st due to high water. Subsequently numerous streets were closed in the City of Brunswick due to closed basin flooding. Closed streets included Chapel Crossing Road, Fairway Oaks Drive, Belle Point Parkway, Fairman Drive, Glynnmarsh Drive, Enterprise Street, Hornet Drive, Shangri-La Avenue and Baybridge Drive. Other flooded areas included Kemble Avenue, Heron Street, N. Cleburn street, Parkwood Street, Wildwood Drive, King Cotton Road, Old Mission road, Key Circle, and Community Road. Several homes in the College Park neighborhood of Brunswick had to be evacuated and had water 6 inches deep inside. The flooding of homes resulted from several days of heavy rainfall. A shelter was opened at Seldon Park on the 2nd.
A retired National Weather Service employee reported 4.55 inches of rain since the previous evening (September 1st) and 2.5 inches of that fell since 700 am EST during the morning of the 2nd.
An off duty NWS employee measured 6 inches of rain since 8 pm EDT last evening. Of that total, 3.25 inches had fallen since 1040 am EDT that day.
Flagler County Emergency Management reported heavy rainfall in Southern Bunnell with 4 to 5 inches of water on U.S. Highway 1.
A spotter reported moderate street flooding along Gate Parkway at the Town Center.
The NWS officially measured 4.11 inches of rainfall which included 2.92 inches that fell in one hour between 11 am and noon.
Three inches of rainfall fell in one hour about 1.5 miles southwest of Interstate 95 and State Road 100.
Emergency Management reported a road washout at Daytona North on Forest Park Road between Evergreen Road and Walnut Road. These were secondary dirt roads.

events.cz_name: ST AUGUSTINE TO FLAGLER BEACH FL OUT 20NM
events.event_narrative: A thin rope waterspout was sighted about 1.5 miles southeast of Flagler Beach.
Lifeguards reported 7 rip current rescues with surf about 2 to 3 feet.
A spotter measured 3.5 inches of rainfall since 2 pm EDT.
A tree was blown down across the road near the intersection of Jamestown Road and U.S. Highway 1.
A spotter measured 5.75 inches of rain overnight.
A spotter reported 2.42 inches of rainfall in one hour (from 9-10 pm EDT).
The creek briefly came out of its banks and flooded backyards, however, the water did not flood West 33rd Street nor any homes.
Law enforcement reported flooding in Hawthorne. Portions of Southeast Highway 301 near County Road 2028 had to be closed due to flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported to the Jesup Press Sentinel that numerous trees and power lines were blown down across Wayne county. The time of the event was based on radar.
The Emergency Manager reported to the Jesup Press Sentinel widespread tree and power line damage across Wayne County due to strong thunderstorm winds.

A lightning strike caused a barn fire in Jamestown. The barn was completely destroyed, but the barn was not in use and ownership of the property was unknown. Another lightning strike also caused extensive damage to the Ware County Sheriff's Department radio equipment, cameras, computers and gate openers. The cost of damage was estimated.

The Clay Electric Company Line Supervisor reported widespread power line damage due to thunderstorm winds across north and northeast portions of Alachua county. Lines were blown down along County Road 235 and County Road 231.

Emergency Management reported a 20 foot diameter sinkhole developed on a private residence driveway near the intersection of Shiloh Road and Randolph Street. A car fell into the hole. The depth of the sinkhole was about 10 feet. No injuries were reported. Radar rainfall estimates ranged from 3 to 5 inches in the area over the past 24 hours.  A tow truck was trying to retrieve the car.
A cooperative observer measured a 24 hour rainfall total of 5.50 inches in High Springs.
The public measured 4.68 inches of rainfall in 24 hours.

The NOS Tide Gage at Mayport reached 6.55 ft. MLLW on the 19th at morning high tide at 9:42 am local time. On the 20th, the gage measured 6.61 ft. MLLW during morning high tide at 10:12 am local time. On the 21st, minor coastal flooding was reported at 4 campsites on the inshore side of Talbot Island around Myrtle Creek. This flooding occurred around the time of high tide since the 19th.
Broadcast media reported a couple was caught in a rip current at Crescent Beach. One person returned to shore; the other drowned.
A business owner along Race Track Road just west of Interstate 95 reported a brief period of penny size hail.

Thunderstorm wind gusts blew down a small barn. Debris from the small barn was blown into a larger barn.  There was substantial damage to the structures, but the cost of damage was unknown. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.

The emergency manager relayed a public report of a funnel cloud in the Jonesville area along State Road 26. A citizen reported a possible touchdown, but the report was unconfirmed and no damage was observed.
The emergency manager relayed several reports of a funnel cloud in the Brooker vicinity along County Road 231. A few unconfirmed reports stated touchdown, but no damage was observed.
Two swimmers were caught in a rip current at south Flagler Beach near the Flagler-Volusia county line. A bystander rescued both people as fire rescue arrived.

The McKinnon St. Simons Island Airport set a new daily rainfall amount of 2.45 inches. Heavy rainfall caused flooding of low lying areas in some portions of the county, including along Buck Swamp Road. A resident of Highland Park along U.S. 341 reported a large oak tree fell on and crushed the back window of her GMC Yukon because the grounds were saturated and soils weak. The cost of vehicle damage was estimated. Utility companies were working to clear debris from drainage ditches.

Lightning struck an outside garage-type building at a Waresboro residence and caused a fire which resulted in about $15,000 in damages. The building had held an antique tractor, a golf cart and a lot of antiques.
The public reported power lines blown down which caused power outages along 156th Place Road in Weirsdale. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.

Thunderstorm winds blew down trees which landed on power lines. Power had to be restored to areas along and near Highway 82 and State Road 110 across eastern Brantley and western Glynn counties by the Okefenokee Rural Electric Membership Corporation. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
A 10-year-old male was struck and injured by lightning in Hawthorne. He was hospitalized.

The tornado first touched down at approximately 1415EST in northwest Pierce County near Merson Road and Crump Road. Several trees were damaged and a farm shed had portions of its sheet metal roof removed. Winds here were estimated to have been near 70 mph or EF-0. The tornado moved northeast across several fields and encountered two small farm structures and a wooded area along Tiny Lane. The structures were completely destroyed with their contents strewn across the wooded area. Extensive tree blow down occurred in the woods with many pines snapped at 10 to 15 feet above ground level.  The tornado was estimated to have been an EF-1 event in this location with winds of 110 mph.  The funnel continued to move across fields next encountering wooded areas and structures near Scuffletown Road. At this point the funnel was one quarter mile or approximately 440 yards wide with winds estimated at 105 mph. Extensive tree blow down continued here with one mobile home destroyed and substantial damage to a wood frame structure.  The tornado crossed the Big Satilla Creek at this point, and crossed into Appling County, continuing on a northeast track.

A National Weather Service storm survey confirmed an EF1  touchdown near 632 Longford Road. At that location trees were overturned and snapped, a swimming pool cage was destroyed and a shed was flipped over onto its side. Winds here were estimated to be 90 mph or EF-1 velocity. The vortex then moved northeast over a wooded area and lake snapping trees. This area was not assessable; however, damage appeared to be in the EF-1 range. The storm then moved over Bethlehem Road downing and snapping trees and power lines. A school bus was also tossed into a ditch near Bethlehem Road and Fender Drive with no injuries and no students onboard. The funnel then struck a shed and mobile home destroying both with debris thrown approximately one quarter mile into the woods. The occupant of the mobile home was tossed from the structure with minor injuries and winds in this area were estimated at 110 mph or strong EF-1 status. The system them moved through a wooded area again snapping trees and crossed Grantham Road near Kicklighter Drive again snapping trees and power lines. Winds were estimated near 90 mph in this area and the vortex lifted off the ground at this point.

A weak tornado intermittently caused damage on a 3 mile path beginning 6 miles east of Douglas.  Most of the damage was snapped tree trunks or limbs, or uprooted trees, but there was minor damage, mainly the roof and one side, to 1 home as well as roof damage to an out-house. A metal roof was peeled off, mangled, and blown toward different directions.

A weak tornado touched down briefly in an open field and tracked northeast, striking a set of chicken houses. Damage was estimated at nearly $3 million to the chicken houses. The structure was primarily made of wood and tin, and amount of damage, mainly to roof of one section, and total collapse of a 2-story section, suggests EF1 damage.   Significant damage to trees was also noted along track.
Ware County Fire Rescue reported power lines down near Beach Road.
A spotter reported a funnel cloud along Highway 158 near the Satilla River.
A spotter reported penny sized hail along highway 158 near the Satilla River.
Large trees were reported to have been blown down and uprooted from thunderstorm winds along Ember Road. Minor property damage also occurred to objects which were left outdoors.
Emergency Management reported numerous trees down along highway 203.
Fire Rescue reported trees blown down along East Lake Drive.

The Emergency Manager reported a roof blown off a house near Live Oak. Damage pictures revealed a weakly constructed section of metal sheet roof was lifted off of a portion of the home by thunderstorm wind gusts. Doppler radar indicated velocities around 40 to 45 knots around 2 to 3 kft agl across the area.  The damage was isolated.
Emergency Management reported some trees and power lines down along State Road 32 west of Nicholls.
The Emergency Manager reported a power line and a few tree tops blown down by thunderstorm wind gusts.
A trained spotter reported a 24 hour rainfall total of 3.51 inches.
Volunteers measured 2.46 and 2.47 inches of rainfall in 24 hrs in Orange Park.
Volunteers in Jacksonville Beach measured 24 hour rainfall totals of 3.82 and 3.85 inches.
Volunteers on the south side of Jacksonville measured 24-hour rainfall amounts of 2.58 to 3.18 inches.
A volunteer measured a 24 hour rainfall total of 2.40 inches.

County emergency management relayed storm total rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches across Palm Coast, with the highest amount of 3.5 inches measured in west-central Palm Coast. Elsewhere across the county, storm total amounts ranged from 3 inches in Bunnell to 4.30 inches in Haw Creek.
Large tree limbs about 4 to 6 inches in diameter were broken and strewn about Nobles Ferry Road, just northwest of downtown Live Oak. The time of the event was based on Doppler Radar imagery.
Sleet and light snow dusted grassy areas and cars from San Mateo to Crescent City and Bostwick. The EMA stated it sleeted for 30 minutes in Crescent City.

The Ocala Police Department reported light sleet around 5:49 am. Snow flurries were reported in Reddick in Northern Marion County around 5:50 am and in Ocala around 6:06 am. By 6:15 am, a HAM Radio operator reported sleet on Interstate 75 about 4 miles southwest of Ocala with minimal collection on the road. Around 6:30 am, a sleet and snow mix covered a car about 5 miles east of Ocala. A accident occurred around 8:15 am due to an icy bridge on the Williams Road Overpass over I-75. No injuries were reported but the bridge was closed for several hours.

Sleet covered a car windshield around 6:15 am in northeast Palm Coast, and was reported by a motorist on Interstate 95 around 6:17 am. By 6:20 am, sleet was reported in Flagler Beach. Around 6:25 am, a locomotive engineer on the Florida East Coast Railway reported steady sleet mixed with snow from Favoritta to Bunnell with a temperature around 31 degrees. More snow reports began around 6:39 am in Palm Coast and continued for several hours from Palm Coast to Bunnell to Flagler Beach. The last report of a sleet and snow mix was around 9:44 am a mile northeast of Bunnell in the Cypress Knoll section of Palm Coast.

Lightning struck a parking lot light at the River City Market Place in front of Best Buy. The concrete base of the light pole was blown out and the parking lot section in front of the store was completely out. No injuries were reported nor damage other than the direct damage to the parking lights was observed. The cost of damage was estimated.

Water flowing over a roadway along State Road 18 near Southwest 115th Court caused a car to drive off the road into a ditch where law enforcement and EMS performed a water rescue of a stranded person under water. The person was not injured.

Alligator Creek overflowed in Starke and caused extensive flooding in Starke. At least one home was damaged due to the creek water. Doppler radar estimated 4 to 5 inches of rainfall within 24 hours in the area.
A funnel cloud was reported over the water east of the St. Augustine Lighthouse.

The county EM received numerous reports of 6 plus inches of rainfall in Southern Columbia county between Ichetucknee Springs State Park and Oleno State Park. Some county roads were briefly impassable. Portions of State Roads 47 and 247 were flooded. At least 5 sinkholes were reported.
Water was reported inside a Subway restaurant in Fort White. Numerous roads were closed in town. A spotter measured storm total rainfall amounts of 6.9 inches in 24 hours.

Flooded roads caused a school bus to partially slide off of the road and into a retention ditch near First Federal Bank off of State Road 207 in Hastings. One child was on the bus and there were no injuries.
Golf ball size hail was reported on Haven Avenue in Green Cove Springs.
Three inches of rainfall occurred in one hour northeast of Keystone Heights.
Four inches of rainfall fell in 3 hours. Minor street flooding was observed.  The emergency manager relayed storm total rainfall reports of 4 to 5 inches across west and northeast Palm Coast.
A cooperative observer measured 4.4 inches of rainfall in 24 hours in Federal Point.

An EF1 tornado touched down around 1322 pm EST in Bradford county. The path width varied from 200 to 400 yards, and the path length was around 9 to possibly 10 miles. Numerous outbuildings were damaged and destroyed. There was mostly minor damage to substantial structures. At least a dozen homes were damaged along County Road 229.  There were 25 homes that suffered minor damage and 28 that had major damage. A total of 23 houses were destroyed. The emergency manager estimated $2.5 to $3 million dollars in damages to homes and about $500,000 in damages to out buildings. The tornado traveled just north of due east and lifted in western Clay County were the path may have gone over the Camp Blanding National Guard Auxiliary.
Large trees were blown down near 94th Street and Highway 49 east of Live Oak.
Several trees were blown down along Highway 90 east of Wellborn.

Central dispatch reported property damage and numerous trees blown down at a residence off of Palm Road. Strong winds damaged a pump house and a water softener. The damage was estimated at one thousand dollars.
A mobile home was flipped over and trees were broken. A shed was destroyed on Southwest Tustenuggee Avenue east of Columbia City.
Power lines and trees were blown down about 3 miles west-northwest of Starke on County Road 225. The power line damage was near 19276 Northwest 63rd Place.
Large tree limbs were blown down near Fort George Island. The time of damage was based on radar imagery.
Large tree limbs were blown down near Fort George Island. The time of damage was based on radar imagery.
Screens on a home were damage along Highway 301 in Lawtey. The top of a maple tree was damaged.
A power line was snapped near Sharron Road. The time of damage was based on radar.
A spotter reported pine trees blown down and a power line blown down along State Road 13, north of State Road 16.
Trees were uprooted along State Road 13, about 3 miles north of Orangedale. The time of the event was based on radar.
The law enforcement reported a tree down on Hernando Drive. The time of the event was based on radar.
Trees were blown down in Penny Farms.
A tree was blown down on a truck on the 2100 block of Mallard Road. The drive had some minor injuries.
About 15 trees were uprooted or snapped off from County Road 315C to Colonial Drive.
A large tree and power lines were blown down across Oakridge Avenue south between Julia and Elsie Streets.
Power lines were blown down per Clay Electric. The time of the event was based on radar.
A tree was blown down along State Road 13 along County Road 208.
Two construction workers were blown off of an overpass. Both men suffered minor injuries.
Numerous large limbs were blown down. Wind gusts were estimated around 60 mph.
Power lines were blown down near 18th Street in East Palatka. The time of the event was based on radar.
Trees and power lines were blown down near 4101 Southeast 26th Court Road.
An EF0  briefly touched down along County Road 121, and winds were estimated around 80 mph. There was significant damage to a mobile home. The cost of damage was unknown.
An EF0 (wind estimated around 80 mph) briefly touched town in Callahan. Semi-tractor trailers were overturned and in trees. The time was based on radar.
Trees were blown down in the Pine Eden area of Marion Oaks.
A spotter reported a funnel cloud with a loud roaring sound as it passed over his location on the south end of the Jennings State Forest. He could hear tree branches and trunks breaking.

events.cz_name: ST AUGUSTINE TO FLAGLER BEACH FL 20 TO 60NM
events.event_narrative: Buoy 41012, about 43 NM east of St. Augustine, measured a wind gust to 52 knots in a thunderstorm.

An EF0 tornado touchdown occurred with winds of 80 mph. Minor damage occurred to a post office and several mobile homes. There was widespread tree damage. An old abandoned brick building was severely damaged.||The Charlton County Herald based in Folkston issued on January 27, 2010, reported a tractor/trailer was damaged at the Woofy Wagon, and several other vehicles were damaged by falling trees or limbs, including one parked at the St. George Post Office and another at a residence. A number of buildings including the laundromat at Rook's had portions of their roofs damaged. One of the crossing arms at the town's main intersection was completely blown off and the knocked askew.
Large tree limbs were blown down onto power lines near Highway 252. The event time was based on radar.
A funnel cloud was spotted southwest of Doctor's Inlet, near Middleburg.

The tornado first touched down at approximately 1415EST in northwest Pierce County near Merson Road and Crump Road. It crossed the Big Satilla Creek, entering into Appling County at this point, and continued on a northeast track. The funnel may have briefly lifted off the ground at this point. The next significant damage occurred along Metts-Overstreet Road with the complete destruction of a singlewide mobile home and a farm shed at approximately 1425EST. Additionally, at this location, a brick cider block structure had one wall knocked over. The tornado then moved into a dairy just west of the intersection of State Road 15 and Wireglass Road. The event was rated as an EF-2 with winds of 135 mph at this location. Three metal building structures were destroyed with one removed from its foundation and blown into a pile of scrap metal. It is possible the funnel may have approached EF-3 at this particular location with winds of 140 to 150 mph; however, other damage to frame and masonry structures at the dairy suggested a lower wind value should be assigned to this area. One individual escaped injury by jumping into a depressed area inside one of the structures before it blew down around her. East of State Road 15, along Wireglass Road, extensive tree blow down and snapping continued in a tree farm. Once again the funnel likely lifted off the ground touching down again at 1430EST near 4230 Antioch Church Road destroying a doublewide mobile home. At this location, two middle aged individuals were in the bedroom, preparing for work, when the funnel destroyed the mobile home. Both escaped with only minor cuts despite the fact that the doublewide was completely obliterated and the frames bent. Once again at this location the winds were rated at 135 mph for a strong EF-2 rating.
Cold air funnels were reported along the U.S. 301 corridor north of Ocala near Sparr.
A horse farm reported that trees were blown down in the area and a heavy grade horse jumping fence was destroyed.

Sporadic reports of sleet began around 11 pm on February 11, 2010, when a trained spotter reported light rain mixed with sleet near Archer. Around 11 am on the 12th, the emergency manager reported light sleet mixed with rain in High Springs. There was no accumulation of sleet.
The public reported light rain mixed with sleet with no sleet accumulation in Ocala.

Sleet was reported from the Jacksonville International Airport by an NWS Employee to Mandarin by a trained NWS storm spotter around 2:09 am. The spotter reported light rain mixed with sleet near the Intersection of I-295 and San Jose Blvd with no accumulation of sleet. The NWS employee reported rain mixed with sleet with no sleet accumulation.
Light sleet was mixed with rain across northern Palatka and portions of northern Putnam county. No accumulation of sleet was reported.
The emergency manager reported light sleet with heavy rainfall about 4 miles NNW of Starke. There was no accumulation of sleet.
Light sleet was mixed with rain on Highway 341 near Interstate 95 about 4 miles NNW of Country Club Estates. There was no accumulation of sleet reported.

Snow was first reported by the emergency manager around 6:17 am in Alma when rain was changing to snow. Around 11:30 am that night, a trained spotter estimated 2 inches of snow about 7 miles north of Alma. Around the same time, county law enforcement reported snowfall accumulations of 1 to 2 inches across the county. Some icy roads were also reported across the county.

Snow was first reported to the NWS around 6:07 pm local time by a NWS spotter. The rain changed to snow in Douglas with minor accumulation noted on cars. Around 11:30 pm that night by the public in Nichols. Around that time 2 to 3 inches of snow had accumulated in the area. The last report of snow in Coffee county was relayed to the NWS in Jacksonville around 2 am on the 13th when a cooperative observer in Pridgen measured 1 inch of snow.

Snow was first reported in Homerville by the county emergency manager around 6:17 pm.  The snow was mixed with rain, and there was no accumulation of snow at the time of the report. Later that evening, around 8 pm, the public reported that all precipitation was now entirely snow in Homerville with no accumulation noted.

Snow become the dominant precipitation type around 6:17 pm per the emergency manager in Pearson and Willacoochee. There was minor accumulation noted on vehicles. By 11:30 pm that night, the county central dispatch reported about 2 inches of snow had accumulated across the county with some icy roadways.
Snow was reported in Millwood around 6:55 pm with no accumulation.
Sleet was first reported in Blackshear by the county emergency manager around 7:03 pm on the 12th. By 2 am on the 13th, a cooperative observer in Patterson measured 1 inch of snow.

Around 8:01 pm, the public reported about a half an inch of snow accumulation on vehicles about 2 miles north of Baxley. By 11:30 pm that evening, county law enforcement reported up to 2 inches of snow across the county. By 2 am on the 13th, a cooperative observer measured 1 inch of snow in Baxley.

Around 8:17 pm, a spotter reported moderate snowfall rates in Jesup. There was light accumulation on vehicles and a dusting on grassy areas. By 11:30 pm, a spotter reported a trace of snowfall in Jesup. The spotter also reported that the snow lasted for about 30 minutes and melted as it fell.
County law enforcement estimated up to 2 inches of snow accumulated across Jeff Davis county around 11:30 pm. Around 2 am, a cooperative observer in Hazelhurst measured 1.3 inches of snow.

events.event_narrative: The buoy measured a wind gust to 59 mph. Also of note was a pressure drop of 11 mb in less than 2 hours around 550 pm that afternoon.
Water was reported in the parking lot and up to car bumpers near Two Way Fish Camp along the Altamaha River around the time of high tide.

Heavy rainfall was first reported in Marion county around 10:15 am by a trained storm spotter who measured 3 inches of rain in 30 minutes time near Rainbow Lakes Estates. Around 12:20 pm a spotter about 3 miles east of Ocala measured 2.25 inches of rain since 8 am. Later around 2:30 pm, a spotter near 103rd Street and 84th Avenue southwest of Ocala measured 6 inches of rainfall between 8 am and 1 pm. At 3 pm, a spotter near Northeast 36th Avenue and Northeast 35th Street recorded 5.85 inches of rainfall between 8 am and 3 pm. At 3 pm, the county emergency manager reported numerous roads were flooded in and near Ocala. At the time, there were no road closures. No property damage estimate was available, but a default of $1,000 was entered which may account for road repair in the wake of the flood.
Several HAM Radio operators saw a funnel cloud near Ocala.
A funnel cloud was sighted at the Fort King Middle School.
Penny size hail was reported in Ocala.
A spotter reported penny size hail on State Road 200 near the Paddock Mall.

Heavy rainfall impacted Flagler county, specifically areas near Bunnell. Around 1:30 pm on March 11th, county emergency management reported 3.30 inches of rain collected at the Emergency Operations Center.  Most of this rainfall occurred between 11 am and 1:30 pm. At the same time, emergency management relayed a report of 2.9 inches of rainfall in East Bunnell since 11 am that morning. By 10 am of March 12th, emergency management measured a 24-hour storm total rainfall amount of 5.01 inches at Haw Creek, which is about 8 miles west southwest of Bunnell.
Two trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds at Marion Oaks. The time of the event was based on radar.

events.event_narrative: Strong winds blew down a tree that damaged two cars and knocked over a light post. The cost of damage was estimated at $4,000. At 11 pm, the Gainesville Regional Airport measured sustained winds of 21 mph and a gust to 40 mph.

A tree was blown down across the road at County Road 80 and Catherine Street in St. Johns Park, which is located about 6 miles west of Bunnell. Another tree was blown down across the road at Martin Luther King Street and South Church Street in Bunnell. The cost of tree removal was estimated.
Power lines were blown down. The report was from the Satilla Rural Electric Membership Corporation.
Trees were blown down along Highway 94.
A funnel cloud was sighted near State Road 207 and U.S. Highway 17.
Nickel size hail was reported at the intersection of Southwest 6th Street and Southwest 3rd Avenue in Gainesville.
Quarter size hail was reported in Suwanee Springs. The time of the event was based on radar.
Penny to half inch size hail was reported 2 miles east of County Road 218 and Highway 301.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Fox Meadows sub-division.
A store clerk reported golf-ball size hail along East Highway 25 just east of Belleview.
Trees were reported blown down near County Road 334A and State Road 26.
Trees were blown down near County Road 337 and State Road 26.
A person was trapped in a home when a tree fell onto the structure along Southeast 73rd Terrace.  The cost of damage was estimated.

Trees, power lines, fences and tree limbs were blown down. There was significant crop damage done. Pea size hail was also observed and 1.62 inches of rainfall fell in about 25 minutes. The cost of crop damage was estimated.
Numerous trees were blown down near the Orange Lake area.
Trees were blown down along Northwest 27th Avenue.
Power lines were blown down along south U.S. Highway 17.
A tree limb was blown down an damaged a car port. The cost of damage was estimated.
Numerous trees were blown down along Highway 26 and Highway 90.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down near Newmans Lake.
Trees were blown down onto a transformer on 600 North Orange Avenue. Trees were blown down onto power lines at 807 Hymon Circle.
Power lines were blown down in East Palatka which caused power outages.
The public reported quarter size hail at 4565 Saddlehorn Trail in Middleburg.
Dime to quarter size hail was observed in Atlantic Beach.
Quarter size hail was reported near White Oak by local business.

events.event_narrative: County emergency management relayed a report from law enforcement of a funnel cloud on Highway 130 between State Road 129 and County Road 47.
Quarter size hail was reported at 1402 SW Tommy Light Street in Fort White.

An approximate seven square mile area of straight line wind damage occurred as a result of a bowing line of thunderstorms. The area of most substantial damage had dozens of large trees uprooted and snapped. A total of 18 structures sustained damage with one mobile home destroyed by a large oak tree that fell through it. Damage indicators suggested maximum winds of around 70 mph. The cost of damage was estimated.
Trees and power lines were blown down in the Three Rivers Estates area.
A tree was uprooted and fell on a home.
A tree was blown down on a home at 3621 NW 18th Terrace.
A tree was blown down onto a trailer with 2 people trapped inside. No injuries were reported.
A tree was blown down on a home at NW 22nd Avenue with no injuries reported.
A barn roof was blown off and into an area of trees. The cost of damage was estimated.

A Cessna plane was flipped at the Gainesville Regional Airport. No injuries were reported. The ASOS at the airport measured a wind gust of 57 mph at the time of damage. The cost of damage was estimated.
A tree fell on a home at 501 NW 30th Avenue. Water damage was occurring in the home at the time of the report due to tree damage.
Trees were blown down across the parking lot at 5830 NW 39th Avenue in Gainesville. Two telephone connection boxes were also damaged. The cost of damage was estimated.

The public reported widespread damage at County Road 325 and Southeast 143 Street. Six large trees were either uprooted or snapped along a quarter mile path. All board fences along the path were blown over and power lines were blown down. The cost of damage was estimated.
The Gainesville Sun reported a car port was destroyed in the Brittany Estates area off of Waldo Road. The cost of damage was estimated.
The Gainesville Sun reported that a woman was trapped inside her home due to trees that were blown down on it. The cost of damage was estimated. No injuries were reported.

An EF1 tornado touched down around 1322 pm EST in Bradford County and continued for a brief period as an EF0 event in Clay County. The path width varied from 200 to 400 yards, and the total path length was around 10 miles. The storm was only present in a small portion of Clay County and entered the Camp Blanding National Guard Facility.
Trees were blown down. One tree broke the window of a mobile home. There were no injuries reported. The time of the event was based on radar.
Trees were blown down along 221st Road. A motorist drove into one tree, but no injuries were reported.
The public reported a funnel cloud near the intersection of U.S. Highway 1 and Race Track Road.
Rainfall of 1.83 inches was measured in 30 minutes. Minor street flooding was observed.
The county emergency operations center rain gauge measured 3.10 inches of rainfall since midnight.
Dime to penny size hail was reported along Highway 441 north of Hazlehurst. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
The Flash Foods store reported quarter size hail. It hailed for 20 to 30 minutes.
Quarter size hail was reported north of Hazlehurst.
Golf ball hail was reported along Satilla Church Road. One vehicle windshield was damaged from the hail. The cost of damage was estimated.
A spotter reported quarter size hail off of Bickley Road. It hailed for 30 to 40 minutes.
Quarter size hail was reported in Mershon along Highway 32.
The Stephen Foster State Park reported that golf ball size hail lasted for 5 minutes and covered the ground. Two large trees were uprooted and other damage was done to Cypress trees.
A tree was blown down at the Twisted Pines Golf Course. Pea size hail was also observed.
About five large trees were blown down across the city of Hazlelhurst.

Thunderstorm winds blew down numerous tress along Orvin Road and County Farm Road. The roof was blown off of a double wide mobile home which caused major damage to the structure. The cost of damage was estimated.
Trees were blown down along J.R. Harper Road. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.

Widespread tree damage was reported along Satilla Church Road and Pat Lewis Road. Trees were blown down on power lines, and trees were blown down along the ground. Some were blown onto structures. No injuries were reported.
Highway 32 had tree damage in Patterson.
Trees were blown down along Highway 32 in Mershon.
Trees were blown down in a residential yard. Hail occurred, the size was unknown. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
Penny size hail was reported along State Road 24 near the Gainesville Regional Airport.
Quarter size hail was reported along Southeast Hawthorne Road.
A local business along County Road 49 reported large tree limbs were blown down. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
An RV Park near Interstate 10 reported several oak and pine trees were blown down. Wind gusts were estimated at 60 mph. The time of the event was based on radar.

About 10 homes from 28 to 44 Esperanto Drive were evacuated due to a wildfire that broke out in the Cypress Knoll area of Palm Coast around 1:30 pm. Vehicles and personnel from surrounding fire departments contained the fire by 4 pm. There were no damage or injuries.
Quarter size hail was reported in the Deep Creek area.
Five trees were blown down along County Road 250 between the Columbia county line and County Road 229. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
Quarter size hail and gusty winds were reported by a local business in Lake Asbury.
A tree was blown down south of the Oklawaha River Country Store along County Road 301.
Employees at the Handy Way food store estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of 60 mph.
A spotter reported penny size hail and some tree debris at the intersection of Interstate 75 and Interstate 10.

Thunderstorm winds damaged property along Shoreline Drive of Orange Lake in Northwest Marion County. Damage included a TV roof antenna that was bent off, a patio cover that was blown about 150 yards into the top of a neighbors tree about 30 feet above ground level, overhangs on the house were destroyed, tree limbs were torn off, and tops of trees were twisted. There was roof damage as well. The time of the event was based on radar. The cost of damage was estimated.
The Oaks and Pines RV Resort reported large tree limbs were broken and feel down due to thunderstorm winds.

A store clerk along U.S. Highway 17 southwest of San Mateo reported quarter size hail. The hail lasted for a short duration. Numerous power outages were reported in the area. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
A spotter measured 4.25 inches of rainfall in 1 hour. The measurement was taken at the intersection of Blanding Blvd. and Aurora Blvd in Orange Park.
A hourly rainfall amount of 2.5 inches was measured in southeast Palm Coast between 10 pm and 11 pm. There was also some street flooding on the northbound lane of U.S. Highway 1 in Bunnell.
Heavy rainfall produced 1.6 inches of rain in 30 minutes in West Palm Coast.
Heavy rainfall of 2.75 inches was measured in Northern Palm Coast.
A lightning strike caused a structure fire in Northern Palm Coast. The cost of damage was estimated.

A funnel cloud was reported near the intersection of State Road 47 and County Road 340 over a corn field. The report was originally relayed as a tornado, but after site inspection there was no damage noted.
Trees and power lines were blown down across Macclenny. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
A home was struck by lightning on Chappie James Court. There was minor structural damage. The cost of damage was estimated.

Lightning stuck three homes in the same neighborhood. The strikes on each home were within minutes of each other. One home on Rolling River Blvd suffered major damage. The other two homes on Crooked River Road and Deep Springs Drive had minor damage. The cost of total damage was estimated.
Thunderstorm wind blew down 3 to 4 small trees about six inches in diameter on the White Oak Plantation property. Dime size hail was also reported.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down across Amelia Island including Amelia City and Fernandina Beach.
A back porch was blown off of a house and landed in the neighbors yard at 7219 Southeast Second Place.
Numerous large tree branches were blown down. Dime size hail was also observed.
Several trees were blown down over Altamaha Park Road near Altamaha Regional Park. Pea size hail was also observed.
Trees were blown down at the Interstate 95 intersection just west of Harriets Bluff.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down in Kingsland near the entrance to the Lakes Subdivision.
Several trees were blown down at the east end of Mush Bluff Road and just west of Crooked River State Park.
A spotter reported penny size hail on Highway 84 just outside of the Blackshear city limits.
Three trees were blown down along Howell Road between Highway 135 and Valentine Road.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down in the Youmans Chapel Area.
Power lines were blown down in the Willacoochee Area.
Penny size hail was reported at the Marion Oaks Golf and Country Club.
One inch hail and tree limbs were blown down about 2.5 miles east-southeast of the Highway 341 and Highway 99 intersection.
A spotter reported quarter size hail at the intersection of State Road 341 and 99. Numerous tree limbs were blown down as well.
Golf ball size hail was reported north of Jesup.
Trees and power lines were blown down at Highway 301 and Harry Jones Road.
The Okefenokee Rural Electric Membership Corporation reported trees and large limbs blown down on power lines south of Woodbine.
Several trees and power lines were blown down on Swamp Perimeter Road.
A small tree and large tree limbs were blown down south of Waycross.
Trees were blown down along Zoar Road.
Large trees were blown down across Denton roads.
A power line was blown down on a shed.
Several trees were blown down on Spell Road.
A large metal fence and trees were blown down n Jesup.
A tree was blown down over State Road 64 outside of Alma.
Trees and power lines were blown down along State Road 221 and Beaver Creek.
Penny size hail was reported on Swamp Perimeter Road.
A large magnolia tree was blown down in Murray Hill.
Power lines and transformers were blown down on Challen Road.
A large tree was blown down on Highway 329 near North Marion High School.

A trail of wind damage was reported from power lines down on Mayflower Street to power lines blown down on Talbot Avenue. Trees were also blown down near the Commonwealth and Edgewood intersection. Roof damage was reported on Edgewater Drive. The cost of damage was estimated. The Perez Ministry building on Edgewood Avenue near Kerle Street had its roof ripped off of the front and thunderstorm winds also knocked down two columns in front of the building.
Large trees were blown down in the Avondale area. The time of the event was based on radar.
A tree and large tree limbs were blown down on Janice Drive north of Hollister.
Several trees and power lines were blown down in the Jesup area. One tree fell on a home on Meadowood Drive. The cost of damage was estimated.
Nickel size hail was reported in Palatka.
Lightning struck a tree at 24066 County Road 247. The cost of removal was estimated.
The AWOS at Naval Air Station Jacksonville measured a wind gust of 60 mph.
Wind damage occurred at 4323 200th Street. Windows were blown out and damage occurred to the exterior of the building. A tree was uprooted. The cost of damage was estimated.
Two trees were blown down in the Silver Meadow Central subdivision.
Trees were blown down near the intersection of Highway 19 and Silver Lake Drive.
Several large trees were blown down at the Lake Oklawaha RV Park. Dime size hail was also reported.
Power lines were down due to blown down trees.
Trees and power lines were blown down.
Power lines were blown down in the Keystone Heights area.
Power lines were blown down near Florahome.
State Road 301 northbound from Gainesville was closed due to flooding. Water was 2 feet deep in some areas on the road.
Trees were blown down just north of the Harriet's Bluff area.
Two trees fell down on two separate homes near the intersection of North Craig Street and the Jacksonville Loop. The cost of damage was estimated.
A tree was blown down on Beauclerc Road and a small tree and power line were blown down on Scott Mill Road.
Trees were blown down along Hamp Chesser Road in Folkston.
The Flash Foods store clerk estimated wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph. The time of the report was based on radar imagery.
Minor flooding was reported in Boone Park. The creek in the park overflowed onto the grassy areas. No property was affected.
Quarter size hail was reported south of Kingsland. Nickel size hail was also observed.
An RV Park employee reported penny size hail.
Penny size hail was reported along Kelly Smith Ranch Road off of West River Road.

Lightning struck a family of 3 that was boating on Thomas Creek on the north side of Jacksonville. One family member was taken to the hospital with life threatening injuries. The other two members were taken to the hospital as a precaution. The time and location were approximated.
Trees and power lines were blown down in Lake Butler.
Trees and power lines were blown down along County road 207A.
Suwannee River State Park official reported several large tree limbs were blown down. The time of the event is based on radar.
Tree limbs were blown down along Kelly Smith Ranch Road off of West River Road.

A waterspout developed over the St. Johns River north of Palatka and was spotted near Racy Point. The spout formed from a low level boundary collision between the east coast sea breeze and outflow from a severe storm moving northward from eastern Putnam County. There were sporadic reports of funnel clouds from U.S. Highway 17 then from State Road 207 around 5:55 pm however locations of the funnel cloud were given in various locations. There was no mesocyclone nor low level rotational signature on Doppler radar and environmental conditions were not favorable for mesocyclone tornadoes (i.e. no wind shear). There was no damage with the vortex and it never made landfall.
Large tree limbs were blown down 1 mile from Crooked River State Park.
Several trees and power lines were blown down in Blackshear. The cost of debris removal was estimated.

Widespread street flooding was reported in downtown Jacksonville and Hogan's Creek overflowed its banks. Water was as deep as 2 feet at the intersection of 1st Street and Pearl Street. Many streets had to be closed for several hours in the evening throughout downtown including Independent Drive near the Modis Building; the intersection of Newman and State Streets; the 1000 Block of North Laura Street; the intersection of East 9th and Walnut Streets and the intersection of West 12th and Davis Streets.
Two brief funnel clouds were spotted near the St. Johns River.
A spotter reported a funnel cloud over the St. Johns River.
A possible funnel cloud was spotted at Fortune Parkway and McLaurin Road not far from the Avenues Mall. This was likely as a thunderstorm outflow converged with the east coast sea breeze in the area.
A spotter reported street flooding at the intersection of Gano Avenue and Debarry Avenue.
A structure fire was caused by a lightning strike on Red Oak Circle. The cost of damage was estimated.
A tree was blown down across Highway 20 across the street from the Tackle Box store.
A large oak tree was blown down across Pine Avenue.
A concrete light pole was blown down at the intersection of Highway 17 and Village Square Parkway.
Nickel size hail was observed in Baxley.
Winds blew down trees along the West Green Highway between Douglas and West Green.
Scattered power lines were blown down across the west side of Baxley. The time of the event was based on radar.
Penny to marble size hail was reported a mile east of Folkston. Gusty winds of 45 to 50 mph were reported.
Water was covering all lanes of Highway 1 in downtown Folkston causing major traffic slowdowns.
A pine tree was blown down across Highway 40. Hail was observed, but the size unknown.
Numerous reports of trees blown down were received by the Charlton County Police Department. One tree fell on a home at 87 Shady Lane in Folkston.
A retired NWS employee reported large tree limbs and small pine trees blown down near Laurel Island Parkway. Winds were estimated between 60 and 70 mph.
A retired NWS employee reported 2 large pine trees snapped off about 10 feet above the ground near the Harrietts Bluff exit of Interstate 95. The time of the event was based on radar.

A flash flood event developed across downtown Jacksonville when two storms collided over the area from the north and south. Around 740 pm, significant street flooding was reported in Riverside then by 755 pm significant flooding was reported in downtown Jacksonville. Areas near Hogans Creek experienced the most flooding. Jefferson Street was closed due to standing water 2 feet deep. At 805 pm, a resident of the Centennial Towers Apartments near Shands Hospital reported Hogans Creek had overflowed its banks and was approaching her apartment. Emergency Management officials reported that the maximum water height was 2 feet from the door of the first floor apartments.
Lightning struck and damaged a building near Oak and Goodwin Streets in the Riverside Area. The building did not catch on fire but it was significantly damaged. The cost of damage was estimated.
Penny size hail was reported in Palm Coast at Old Kings Road and Fanshawe Lane. The time of the event was based on radar.
A spotter measured 1.6 inches of rainfall from 4 pm to 5 pm. There was pooling of water and flooded ditches along Argyle Forest Blvd between Old Middleburg Road and Shindler Drive.
A spotter measured 1.42 inches of rainfall in 45 minutes. A 42 mph wind gust was also measured along with small limbs down.
Trees were blown down and blocking the road at Old Kings Road near Interstate 95.
Two trees were blown down along I-295 on the Jacksonville Westside between 103rd Street and Blanding Blvd. The time of the event was based on radar.
Quarter size hail was reported at the corner of Kight Street and Wiregrass Street in Homerville. Half inch size hail was also observed.
Trees were blown down on the Cogdell Highway northeast of Homerville.
A structural fire was started by lightning. The fire was ongoing at the time of the report. The event time was based on radar, and the cost of damage was estimated.

The Gainesville Regional Airport measured a wind gust of 22 knots with an outflow boundary that moved northward from a storm complex that was dissipating over Marion County. One tree was blown down and blocked one lane of traffic on Schoolhouse Road in southwest Gainesville The time of the event was based on radar, and the cost of damage was estimated.
A tree was blown down on East Dame Avenue. Residents reported other trees down in the area.
Large tree limbs were blown down across roadways southeast of Jesup.
A tree was blown down near Lucille Drive. The time of the event was based on radar.
A tree was blown down at a residence which damaged the car and caused a power outage at the home. The time of the event was based on radar. The cost of damage was estimated.
Trees were blown down on Lake Drive.
Power lines were blown down near downtown Nicholls.
Trees were blown down about a mile southeast of Fargo near the intersection of Highway 441 and Highway 94. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
A spotter reported dime to nickel size hail and four inches of storm total rainfall. Wind gusts to 55 mph were also estimated.
A spotter measured 2.6 inches of rainfall in under one hour. The time frame of the event was estimated.
Quarter size hail was reported along U.S. Highway 301 by a store clerk. The time of the event was based on radar.
The REACT base station in Northwest Palm Coast measured 2.25 inches of rainfall in 50 minutes. The report was from Bunker Hill Drive.
A large oak tree was blown down in the Raley Creek area of Arlington near Raley Creek Drive East and Creekview Drive. The time of the event was based on radar.
Large tree limbs were blown down northeast of Ocala at the intersection of Northeast 34th Street and Northeast 30th Court.

A couple of pecan trees were blown down near the intersection of Post Road and Chicora Road. One tree fell on a house and the other on a car. The cost of damage was estimated, and there were no injuries reported.

The St. Augustine Record reported a house fire caused by a lightning strike on the 2200 block of Clovelly Lane off of County Road 210 around 5 pm local time. Firefighters contained a small fire that originated in the home's attic. There were no injuries, and there was only minor damage. The cost of damage was estimated.
A light pole was blown down in Willacoochee.
Trees were blown down along Matthew Road. The time of the event was estimated based on radar imagery.
Trees were blown down along County Road 231 near Northwest 192nd Avenue, north of Gainesville.
A tree fell through a roof at 1012 Northwest 51st Terrace. The cost of damage was estimated.
Trees were blown down in Trenton. One was blown down on a car, and one was blown down on a house. The cost of damage was estimated.
Numerous trees were blown down between Luraville and County Road 250.
A tree was blown down near the intersection of County Road 235 and Southwest 161st Street. The time of the event was based on radar.
Many trees were blown down along Old Axson Road, and yard debris was blown across Highway 441 north of Pearson.
Large tree limbs were blown down. The time of the event was based on radar.
Scattered reports of blown down trees occurred across the Gainesville city limits between 430 pm and 6 pm local time.
A tree was blown down across Millhopper Road. The event time was based on radar.
A tree was blown down across Southwest 82nd Way. The event time was based on radar.
A tree was blown down across NW 47th Lane.

Extensive tree damage occurred in Nicholls between 530 pm and 6 pm local time as a gust front moved through from the northwest and a strong low level rotation traversed the city from the north. After the emergency manager conducted a survey, it was determined that the damage was downburst related. There were several reports of trees that were blown down on cars, and 7 homes suffered damage from trees. The cost of damage was estimated.
Power lines were blown down near Bulow Plantation Ruins Historic State Park. The time of the event was based on radar imagery.
Trees were blown down into power lines. The fire department was dispatched because residents detected smoke, but a fire did not develop.

The combination of heavy rainfall, water pooling on the roof and structural failure caused the roof of the Family Dollar Store on 4420 Altama Avenue in the Brunswick area to collapse. One person was hospitalized due to injuries and 3 others suffered minor injuries. Radar indicated rainfall rates near 2 inches per hour, and the time of the event was estimated. The cost of damage was estimated at $20K and the cost of supply damage was estimated at $10K.
A REACT volunteer measured 2.45 inches of rainfall in one hour.
The Atkinson County 911 Dispatch relayed a public report of a funnel cloud in Pearson.
A spotter on Summer Breeze Drive in north Jacksonville measured 2.25 inches of rainfall in 1.5 hours.

The Jacksonville Beach Life Guard station performed a total of 6 rip current rescues over the weekend. One near drowning occurred around 8:30 am in the morning at Jacksonville Beach before the life guards were on duty. The woman was rescued by Jacksonville Beach Fire Rescue then taken to the hospital in critical condition.
Breakers of 5 to 8 feet were reported along Flagler Beach. Heights as high as 10 feet were occasionally observed.
Breakers of 4 to 6 feet were observed with occasional 8 foot breakers.
Power lines were blown down across Jacksonville Beach.

events.cz_name: FERNANDINA BEACH TO ST AUGUSTINE FL OUT 20NM
events.event_narrative: The public reported a waterspout east of Neptune Beach.

The Arabia Bay wildfire burned within a peat swamp for most of the month of November. The fire grew from 500 acres on Nov. 14th to 700 acres on the 15th. On the 19th, the fire was approximately 1170 acres. On the 23rd the fire had grown to 2688 acres and was about 75% contained. By the 25th, the fire was 100% contained and had reached 2710 acres in size. The fire had produced significant amounts of smoke over a large portion of southern Georgia and north Florida. This smoke and fog indirectly resulted in an injury to a Sheriff's Officer due to a traffic accident.||Heavy ash and smoke were reported near the fire, and depending on the wind regime, some days very heavy smoke impacted Atkinson and Bacon counties  (north of the fire site). Smoke was the major impact from the fire as property was not threatened. There were no injuries reported to the NWS that were fire related. There were several road closures due to smoke near the fire. ||The fire burned through the end of the month and into December. The NWS Jacksonville provided daily site specific fire weather forecasts, spot forecasts and ran Hysplit runs and disseminated this data to the GEMA Area Coordinator as well as created a web site for fire response officials to reference. ||On Nov. 23rd, the total cost spent on fire control was $230,672. This amount does not include property damage to swampland.

Lightning directly hit the Pierce County Emergency Operations Tower. The strike traveled down the tower and severely damage the center's control box for the tower, its server, radio for both the county EMS and Pierce County jail as well as radios for dispatch stations and telephone lines. The Honey Prairie Wildfire complex engulfed much of the Okefenokee Swamp during the month of May 2011. On May 1st, the fire burned about 750 acres. By the evening of May 6th, the fire had burned about 29,852 acres. On May 10th, the fire burned 19,521 acres in 24 hrs, which damaged a total of 81,434 acres. On the 18th, the fire had burned 146,924 acres and was 55 percent contained. Stephen Foster State Park and Swamp Island Drive at the Okefenokee Swamp East Entrance were closed on the 18th. By the 20th, the fire was 66 percent contained. By the 23rd, the fire had consumed 148,424 acres and was 70 percent contained. On the 28th the fire remained 70 percent contained and has burned 149,550 acres.  Stephen Foster State Park remained closed.

The of fire containment was estimated to be around $45M.  During the life of the fire, about 90 residences and 25 commercial properties were threatened. There were about 196 other buildings and structures threatened, with only one documented loss from the fire per the July 25th Incident Status Summary.

The Racepond wildfire was about 5 miles NNW of Race Pond in Brantley County, Ga.  The fire had burned 20,934 acres on the 4th and was 75 percent contained. On the 17th, the fire was about 92 percent contained. The fire threatened 300 residences and 400 outbuilding, however there was no documented loss nor damage according to the Incident Status Summary issued on the 17th. Total cost for fire suppression and containment was about $5M.

The Sweat Farm Again Wildfire was about 3 miles SW of Waresboro in Ware County, Ga. On the 5th, the fire had burned about 19,169 acres and was 75 percent contained. On the 17th, the fire was 92 percent contained. The Incident Status Summary (ISS) issued on the 17th for the fire indicated that it had threatened about 200 residences, damaged 1, and destroyed 2. There were about 300 outbuildings threatened and 11 were destroyed.  The cost to mitigate the fire was about $3M per the ISS on the 17th.

The Espanola Wildfire was about 5 miles NE of Andalusia in Flagler County Florida. On the 1st, the fire had burned 5,136 acres and was 70 percent contained. By the 7th, the wildfire was 75 percent contained.

Tropical storm force wind gusts began around noon, 12:03 pm, on the 27th across Duval county. At this time, the ASOS station at Craig Airfield measured a wind gust to 39 mph. At 3:15 pm, the Jacksonville Beach Pier measured sustained winds of 35 mph with gusts to 55 mph. At 6:25 pm the Mayport Naval Station ASOS measured a gust to 48 mph. At 6:49 pm, Craig Airfiled in Arlington measured a wind gust to 46 mph in a rain band. At 8:30 pm, the Jacksonville Beach Pier Mesonet site measured a wind gust of 56 mph. At 8:30 pm, a Mesonet site at Huguenot Park measured a sustained wind of 54 mph with a gust to 63 mph. At 8:47 pm, the Mayport Naval Station ASOS measured a gust to 58 mph in a rain band. At 9 pm, broadcast media reported that the Wonderwood Expressway was shut down in both directions near A1A after a light pole was blown down across the road. At 9:20 pm, local broadcast media reported a roof was blown off a home on Hecksher Drive, about 3 miles NW of Fort Caroline. At 9:30 pm, broadcast media reported a tree was blown down on a home on the 700 block of Arlet Drive. The time of this damage was based on radar. At 9:36 pm, Craig Airport measured a gust to 58 mph. At 9:48 pm, Naval Air Station Jacksonville measured a wind gust to 60 mph. At 10 pm, the mesonet station on Buck Island measured a gust to 67 mph, this is about 4 miles west of Mayport on the St. Johns River south bank. At 10:05 mph, a wind gust to 56 mph was measured at the Jacksonville International Airport by the ASOS station. At 10:30 pm, an NWS employee reported a large tree was blown down and blocking Stowe Run Lane in Arlington. At 10:35 pm, the Buck Island mesonet site measured a gust to 73 mph (highest known measured speed for Beryl). At 10:35 pm, the mesonet site at Huguenot Park measured sustained winds of 50 mph with gusts to 60 mph. At 10:37 pm, Naval Air Station Jacksonville measured at 65 mph wind gust. At 11:00 pm, the Jacksonville Electric Authority reported about 18,000 power outages in the Jacksonville area of Arlington. At 11:10 pm, as mesonet site about 4 miles west of Mayport measured sustained winds NNE at 47 mph with gusts to 62 mph. ||Rough surf and flooding reports started during the early morning hours of the 28th across Duval county. At 12:50 am, an off duty NWS employee reported rough surf around 6 feet and water up to the dune line at Jacksonville Beach. At 9:45 am, minor flooding was reported in San Marco, about a foot lower than the water height from TS Fay, per an NWS employee observation. At 10:43 am, an NWS employee reported flooding at 1596 Lancaster Terrace at the Broadview Towers Condominium. The St. Johns River rose similar to TS Fay at this location. A below ground parking lot was completely flooded with three cars floating. The river was breaking over the sea wall. Peak flooding at this location occurred between 4 am and 5 am earlier in the morning. At 10:43 am, flooding was reported at the corner of Copland and River Blvd in Jacksonville Beach. Parts of the seawall were ripped off and moved 8 to 12 feet. A dock was destroyed and debris was over the area. The peak flooding at this location was around 5 am to 6 am. ||During the afternoon heavy rainfall amounts from Beryl across Duval county included at 3:18 pm report from broadcast media of storm total rainfall amounts thus far of 4.05 inches at I-295 and Gate Parkway. At 4:16 pm, the broadcast media reported over 6 inches of measured rainfall thus far on Debutante Drive in Arlington.

At 3:13 pm on the 27th, the county emergency management agency reported a tree was blown down on power lines on Forest Hill Drive in Palm Coast. At 9:42 pm on the 27th, trees were blown down on a power line at North 18th St. and Central Ave. in Flagler Beach. At 12:41 pm on the 28th, storm total rainfall amounts in Palm Coast were 5.43 in northern Palm Coast to 5.25 inches in east Palm Coast. Elsewhere in Palm Coast rain totals ranged from 2.25 inches in west-central Palm Coast to 4 inches in west Palm Coast.

At 8:45 pm the NOS Buoy at Fernandina Beach reported a storm surge of 3.47 feet. At 9:35 pm, the emergency manager reported a telephone pole and power lines were blown down on Norris St. between Alexander and Church Streets in St. Marys. At 10:35 pm that evening, the broadcast media reported wind damage to a beach condo in Fernandina Beach.
